h1: The 6 Best OLED TVs of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: six OLED TVs from LG and Samsung, from 42 to 77 inches, sorted by room size, series and who each set is best for.
summary: OLED listings share the same headline specs, so size and series decide the ranking. The LG 65 inch C6 is our top pick as the current-generation mainstream set. The Samsung 65 inch S90H is the alternative brand, the LG 55 inch C5 is the prior-year value, and the LG 42 inch C6 suits desks and small rooms.
intro: The common mistake is comparing OLEDs by brand and ignoring the series year. A C5 and a C6 look similar on a shelf, but the newer series is the one you should compare first.

We reviewed eight listings and ranked six on series, size, platform and price bucket. The listings mostly give size, panel type and Dolby Atmos, so we rank on those and avoid claims about picture performance we cannot back.

products.name: LG 65-Inch Class OLED evo AI 4K C6 Series Smart TV w/Dolby Atmos
products.verdict: The current C6 series in the most popular size, with Dolby Atmos.
products.description:
This is LG's 65 inch OLED evo C6 with AI features, 4K resolution and Dolby Atmos support, in the $500+ bucket.

It leads because 65 inches suits most living rooms and the C6 is the newer series in this list. The Samsung S90H competes at the same size.

Buy it for a main living room set. The caveat is that the listing says little about brightness.

products.name: Samsung 65-Inch Class S90H Series
products.verdict: Samsung's S90H OLED at 65 inches, the cross-brand alternative.
products.description:
The Samsung S90H in 65 inches is an OLED set in the $500+ bucket. The listing is brief, naming the series, size and panel type.

It ranks second because the LG listing gives more detail, including the Dolby Atmos support. Choose between them by interface preference.

It suits Samsung households. The caveat is the thin listing.
products.skipIf: You want a detailed spec sheet.

products.name: LG 55-Inch Class OLED evo AI 4K C5 Series Smart TV w/Dolby Atmos
products.verdict: The previous-generation C5 in 55 inches, often the value route.
products.description:
The C5 in 55 inches is an OLED evo 4K set with AI features and Dolby Atmos, in the $500+ bucket.

It ranks third because it is the older series and a smaller panel, though older series often cost less. It matches the C6 on listed features.

It suits medium rooms. The caveat is checking whether the price actually is lower.

products.name: Samsung 55-Inch Class S90H Series
products.verdict: Samsung's S90H in a smaller 55 inch size.
products.description:
The 55 inch S90H is an OLED set in the $500+ bucket, with the same short listing as its larger siblings.

It ranks fourth since the LG C5 gives more listed detail at the same size. It is the right pick for Samsung loyalists with a smaller room.

It suits bedrooms. The caveat is the sparse spec text.

products.name: LG 42-Inch Class OLED evo AI 4K C6 Series Smart TV w/Dolby Atmos
products.verdict: The only 42 inch OLED here, for desks and small rooms.
products.description:
This 42 inch C6 is an OLED evo 4K set with AI features and Dolby Atmos, in the $500+ bucket.

It ranks fifth because few rooms want a 42 inch TV, yet it is the only compact choice here. It is the smallest way into the newer C6 series.

It suits a desk, bedroom or small apartment. The caveat is paying premium money for a small screen.
products.skipIf: You sit far from the screen.

products.name: Samsung 77-Inch Class S90H Series
products.verdict: A 77 inch OLED for big walls and dedicated viewing rooms.
products.description:
The 77 inch S90H is the largest OLED in this roundup, in the $500+ bucket, with the same brief listing as the other S90H models.

It ranks last because 77 inches suits few rooms and the listing gives little to separate it from smaller siblings. For a large wall it is the only size jump here.

It suits a home theater. The caveat is wall width and viewing distance.

methodology.title: Series generation
methodology.description: Newer series ranked above older ones at the same size.

methodology.title: Size range
methodology.description: We covered 42 to 77 inches to suit different rooms.

methodology.title: Listing detail
methodology.description: Listings naming Dolby Atmos and AI features ranked higher.

methodology.title: Brand variety
methodology.description: Both LG and Samsung are represented.

methodology.title: Price bucket
methodology.description: All sets sit in the $500+ bucket, so it did not separate them.

whatMatters.detail: Size depends on viewing distance. Sit about 1.2 to 1.6 times the diagonal away for 4K. Measure the wall and seat distance before choosing.
LG names series like C5 and C6, with the higher number newer. Newer series may bring updates, older ones often cost less. Check the model name in the title.
OLED lights each pixel, so blacks are deep. Static images over very long periods are a known risk, so vary content. Confirm OLED is named in the listing.
Dolby Atmos support is listed on the LG models. It matters if you use a soundbar. Look for it in the title.
Samsung listings here are brief. Check the manufacturer page for ports and refresh rates before buying.

howToChoose.intro: Start with the wall and seating distance.

cards.label: LG
cards.text: Listings name OLED evo, AI and Dolby Atmos. The C6 and C5 models are LG.

cards.label: Samsung
cards.text: The S90H listings are brief but cover 55, 65 and 77 inches.

howToChoose.note: Most buyers should default to LG for the clearer spec sheet unless they prefer Samsung's interface.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A 42 to 55 inch size and good dark-room performance from OLED.

cards.label: In this ranking
cards.text: The LG 42 inch C6 and 55 inch C5 fit, and the Samsung 55 inch S90H is an alternative.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You want the newest series or the largest screen, pointing to the LG C6 or Samsung 77 inch.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: Last year's series is fine, in which case the LG 55 inch C5 is the likely value.

faq.a: OLED panels light each pixel individually, allowing deep blacks. It differs from LED-backlit TVs.
Static images shown for very long periods can cause it, so vary content and use screensavers.

faq.q: Is a C6 worth it over a C5?
faq.a: Only if the price gap is small. Listings show similar headline features.
Choosing size without measuring viewing distance.

faq.q: How do I set one up?
faq.a: Mount or stand it, connect WiFi and your soundbar, then pick a picture mode for your room.

faq.q: Why did you leave out a few sizes?
faq.a: We dropped duplicate sizes of the same series to keep the roundup varied.

finalTake: The LG 65 inch C6 is the best OLED TV for most living rooms. The Samsung 65 inch S90H is the alternative brand, the LG 55 inch C5 is the likely value, and the 42 inch C6 suits small spaces. Check manufacturer pages for details these listings omit.
